by.claim: The "1 in 6 Helm-parameter-only RollingSync rollouts" figure in T-27949 is unobservable in production: the ticket itself says there is no counter that increments when `specChanged` fires without a resulting sync operation, so the number is a headcount of support pings. The metrics request that would be the natural home for that counter, T-27846, asks for four progressive-sync measurements (time from detection to trigger, time to complete step X, how many Application refreshes the ApplicationSet caused, and which Applications a stalled sync is waiting for) and none of them counts a spec change that produced no sync operation. Shipping T-27846 as proposed therefore leaves the T-27949 failure mode exactly as unmeasured as it is today.

The roadmap's sharding schedule depends on an unmeasured close condition without saying so: strategy.md states that application controller capacity is committed to the Progressive Sync Stable-promotion punch list and that sharding will not start until the Stable promotion closes, while T-28927 defines that punch list only as open enhancement and bug label queries. Because closure is judged from ticket queues rather than any observable behavior, and the progressive-sync observability that would tell anyone whether the feature is behaving, T-27846, is itself still an open request, there is no measurement that can say when the punch list is actually done, and therefore none that can date the start of sharding.

distractorGate.note: DX1/DX2 violations fail rung 3 for runs scored from this date; score files recorded earlier are never regenerated and keep their as-run results. Evidence: five distractor-disciplined runs (two single-pass, three composed dispatch-shape) all clean; every run before the discipline paragraph violated at least one.
